GK04-q01-vmfste: Out-of-service orders are real, but safety for everyone is the top reason to inspect.
Avoiding costly breakdowns is a benefit, but safety is the most important reason.
GK04-q02-zxhn65: 5/32 inch is above the 4/32 front-tire minimum, so this tire passes.
Rear tires need only 2/32 inch, so 3/32 passes.
GK04-q03-rooorq: Rust around wheel nuts is a warning that they may be loose, not a sign of a recent change.
A welded rim is a separate defect; rust around the nuts points to loose nuts.
GK04-q04-xomvwv: The handbook's line is more than 10 degrees (about 2 inches on a 20-inch wheel), not 5.
The line is more than 10 degrees; waiting for 15 would let too much play pass.
GK04-q05-3jrmvr: Missing ¼ or more of the leaves means out-of-service, cracked or not.
The suspension always carries weight; ¼ missing is out-of-service loaded or empty.
GK04-q06-78q8fg: A charged, rated fire extinguisher is one of the three required items.
Warning devices for parked vehicles are one of the three required items.
GK04-q07-xh2qrj: You need 3 red reflective triangles, not 2.
6 is the number of fusees; reflective triangles are 3.
GK04-q08-ny8ytm: The ABS light should go out right after start-up; staying on means a fault.
The trailer's ABS lamp is on its left rear and works the same way; a light that stays on means a fault.
GK04-q09-t6ddf5: 3 minutes is the time for air to build 50 to 90 psi, not oil pressure.
Temperatures rise gradually; oil pressure must come up within seconds.
GK04-q10-znude8: 45 seconds is the Air Brakes section's dual-system figure; section 2.1 says 3 minutes.
The section 2.1 standard is 50 to 90 psi within 3 minutes, not 2.
GK04-q11-4l1hd1: The engine is already off; the key goes with you so no one can start or move the truck.
The handbook says you take the key with you, not hand it to the examiner.
GK04-q12-fjfrez: Red is for rear lights and reflectors; the front clearance lights must be amber.
White is allowed only for front turn signals; front clearance lights are amber.
GK04-q13-auxk84: Wrench-testing is for rust-streaked lug nuts; bearing seals are checked for leaks.
Rust streaks are looked for at the lug nuts; bearing seals are checked for leaks.
GK04-q14-n2pgvh: The numbers are swapped: pump 3 times, then hold 5 seconds.
Driving at 5 mph is the service brake test, not the hydraulic leak test.
GK04-q15-s4mjz7: There is no 25-mile rule; the first cargo check is within 50 miles.
150 miles is for the repeat checks that come after the first one at 50 miles.
GK04-q16-dg5e2a: At 60 mph you reach 150 miles in 2.5 hours, and whichever comes first applies.
Cargo must be rechecked during the trip, every 150 miles or 3 hours.
GK04-q17-fjqcfc: The handbook says the copy stays in the vehicle for 1 day, not a week.
The handbook asks only that a copy of the after-trip report stay in the vehicle for 1 day.
GK04-q18-urroia: Once you drive, safe operation is your job, not the mechanic's.
The carrier certifies repairs, but the driver is responsible for safe operation.
GK04-q19-llpipm: Leaking shock absorbers are on the suspension defect list.
Cracked torque rods are a suspension defect; they help hold the axle in place.
GK04-dn-5vwv89: 2/32 inch is for tires other than the front; front tires need 4/32.
3/32 inch is below the 4/32 front-tire minimum.
GK04-dn-8q8g88: 4/32 inch is the front-tire rule; other tires need only 2/32.
The handbook's figure for non-front tires is 2/32 inch, not 3/32.
GK04-dn-vngxkf: Radials aren't banned; mixing radial and bias-ply tires is the problem.
4/32 inch meets the front-tire minimum, so it's allowed.
GK04-dn-brlsly: 2 is the inches of play at the rim of a 20-inch wheel; the limit is 10 degrees.
20 is the wheel size in the example; the play limit is more than 10 degrees.
GK04-dn-xuolm2: The out-of-service line is ¼ of the leaves, not half.
Just ¼ missing puts it out-of-service, and any defect can be dangerous.
GK04-dn-i0kzq3: 3 is the number of triangles or liquid-burning flares; fusees are 6.
GK04-dn-lcywva: 35–75 psi is normal operating oil pressure, not idling.
50–90 psi is the air pressure build-up check, not oil pressure.
GK04-dn-ulk7ad: 85–100 psi in 45 seconds is the Air Brakes dual-system figure, not section 2.1's.
120–140 psi is the usual governor cut-out, not the 3-minute build range.
GK04-dn-sps740: 50–90 psi is the 3-minute build check, not governor cut-out.
35–75 psi is normal operating oil pressure, not air pressure.
GK04-dn-5i5vd2: 3 is the number of pumps; you then hold the pedal 5 seconds.
45 seconds is an Air Brakes build-up time; the hydraulic hold is 5 seconds.
GK04-dn-hszmuo: The service brake test is done at about 5 mph, not 30.
60 mph is far too fast for this test; drive about 5 mph.
GK04-dn-ap20xq: At 30 mph, 150 miles takes 5 hours, so the 3-hour limit comes first.
50 miles is only for the first check; after that it's 150 miles or 3 hours.
GK04-dn-l6miha: The handbook asks only that a copy of the after-trip report stay in the vehicle for 1 day.
3 hours is part of the cargo check interval; the report copy stays 1 day.
GK04-dn-g1s99s: Amber is for front lights and reflectors; rear ones are red.
White is allowed only for front turn signals; rear clearance lights are red.
